checks.note: API docs: Bearer token in Authorization header, ipx_live_ prefix; MCP docs add ipx_test_ sandbox and dashboard keys. OAuth2 mentioned only for planned QuickBooks/Stripe integrations, not API auth. Per-IP unauthenticated MCP use confirmed on GitHub README.

Homepage: 'Upgrade to the 100-audit Credit Pack or Unlimited for API access'. Pricing page does not say which tier includes API, as the record states. Prices ($99 pack, $299/mo) match. Forensic report is $297 on pricing vs $199 in MCP docs, as the record notes.
API docs list exactly 3 REST endpoints (POST /audit, GET /rates, POST /audit/document) on a supabase.co base URL; no quota stated, only 429 on 60s window. Narrow is correct.

GitHub README (iPAYX-Technologies/mcp-fx-audit) declares iPayX as operator with remote endpoint https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp; homepage lists a native MCP server. MCP docs list a supabase.co endpoint instead, so the conflict is real. Operator claim is self-declared in the README.

ready_with_caveats is consistent: the API works with keys but the plan that includes API is unstated, docs conflict on MCP endpoint and report price ($297 vs $199), and no rate limit quota is documented.

corrected.one_liner: iPayX Protocol is a FINTRAC-registered FX forensic audit service that scores FX transactions against live mid-market rates to flag hidden markup, spread and fees.
corrected.auth_notes: Static API keys sent as Authorization: Bearer. Prefixes ipx_live_ (production) and ipx_test_ (sandbox). No OAuth documented for API access (OAuth2 appears only for planned QuickBooks/Stripe integrations). Some MCP tools work unauthenticated (per-IP free limits).
corrected.access_notes: Homepage says API access comes with the Credit Pack or Unlimited tiers. Pricing page lists Free (3 lifetime audits), Credit Pack 100 at $99 one-time, Unlimited at $299/mo, and a Full Forensic FX Report at $297 one-time; it does not say which tier includes API keys. Keys are generated in the dashboard after sign-in. Some MCP tools need no signup.
corrected.blocker: Narrow API (3 REST endpoints: POST /audit, GET /rates, POST /audit/document). The API-key tier is unclear, and the pricing page shows no explicit API plan. The vendor's own docs conflict on MCP endpoint (mcp.ipayx.ai vs a supabase.co URL) and on the forensic report price ($297 vs $199). The REST base URL is on supabase.co. The rate limit quota is undocumented.
